summary: The agent reported all five questions as answered and asked for headline approval while the user had seen the numbers behind only one of them; Q2 used the identified-revenue denominator alone and guest revenue was given only as a percentage.
evidence: A2, U3, A3; feedback/human.md pain point 1; human/notes.md Turn 3; feedback/agent.md section 5
tag_reason: The status line convention ('N answered' means recorded) and the headline-only preview format are workbench behaviour that any interactive user would meet.

summary: Packaging and release carry heavy instruction volume and four full independent reviews, including a fresh full re-review at release when the reviewed candidate had not changed, making packaging the slowest phase.
evidence: A5 (13.3 min), A6, A7; feedback/agent.md 1.1 and 5; feedback/harness-log.md; project/investigations/marketing-investment/package-reviews/
tag_reason: The review gates and contract size come from the released awb-package/awb-release skills, not from the simulation setup.

summary: The draft and finding number checks flag dates, a citation year, compact count/rate pairs and source counts as unrecorded numbers, forcing prose rewrites around the checker.
evidence: A3 and A5; feedback/agent.md 1.2 and section 3; feedback/agent-notes.md (seasonality-comparison warning, check-draft numeric rows)
tag_reason: The records/state finding and package check-draft helpers raised these warnings on sound prose.

summary: The awb read SQL tool reports unbound prepared-statement parameters as a read-only plan-safety refusal and advises running without --read-only.
evidence: A2; feedback/harness-log.md (awb/read failure); feedback/agent.md 1.3 and section 3
tag_reason: The error text and missing parameter binding come from the released MCP read tool and would appear on any host.

summary: Because awb-status is read-only, slide edits the user sent in the same message as the status request were not recorded until a separate awb-package request, costing a turn.
evidence: U4, A4, U5; feedback/human.md pain point 3; feedback/agent.md 1.4
tag_reason: The read-only rule is in the awb-status skill, and the README does not warn that combined edits wait.

summary: The agent linked and quoted internal SKILL.md files in its messages to the user to justify pauses, which the user found irrelevant and could not open.
evidence: A1, A4, A6; feedback/human.md pain point 2; human/notes.md Turns 2, 5, 7
tag_reason: It could be a Codex habit or a skill instruction to name the rule when pausing; the release text was not inspected to tell which.

summary: The README presents clean and explore as steps, but the agent folded them into answering, leaving the user unsure whether something was skipped.
evidence: A2, U3; feedback/human.md pain point 6 and section 3; human/notes.md Turn 3
tag_reason: The README sets the step expectation, and the release does not say when cleaning and exploring are folded into analysis.

summary: awb-clean would have required a user choice over which rows win even for the proven exact 22,523-line overlap between the two sheets, so the agent bypassed it with a per-investigation sheet split.
evidence: A2; feedback/agent.md 1.5 and section 4; feedback/agent-notes.md (scope settled entry)
tag_reason: This is the agent's reading of the released awb-clean skill and would apply on any host.

summary: awb-init cannot create an investigation before the first scope interview, so the rich intake had to be parked in the project README.
evidence: A1; feedback/agent.md 1.5 and section 2; feedback/agent-notes.md (initial setup entry)
tag_reason: The ordering is set by the released awb-init and awb-scope skills.

summary: The package contract's required title, answer, findings, methods and caveats sections produce nine content slides against an 'about 8 slides' request; the agent resolved it as 8 main slides plus an appendix.
evidence: A2 headline preview; feedback/agent.md 1.6
tag_reason: The slide structure comes from the released package contract and deck rules.

summary: The first full draft described the company as a 'UK online retailer' and labelled chart sources as the UCI export, so the user had to correct identity and source wording.
evidence: U6 items 1-2; feedback/human.md section 6; feedback/agent.md 1.13
tag_reason: Both come from a public dataset standing in for the persona's own export; a real company export would not carry a UCI identity or label.

summary: The first draft used technical control-group wording, imperative 'How we know' bullets (after the slide-8 headline had already been corrected) and an undefined repeat-buyer metric, needing user corrections.
evidence: U6 items 3-6, A6; feedback/human.md section 6; feedback/agent.md 1.13
tag_reason: Partly the Codex agent's drafting and partly the templates and review rules not prompting for plain language or declarative methods; the split cannot be determined from the logs.

summary: The scope interview did not ask about non-product stock codes; the user raised them, and the agent then gave a good recommendation.
evidence: U2, A2; feedback/human.md pain point 4; human/notes.md Turn 2
tag_reason: The interview ran before the data was landed, and the persona volunteered the codes before the agent's data checks surfaced them, so a real user's experience cannot be inferred.

summary: Replies were long and repeated content: scope questions listed twice, confirmation asked twice, and a lot of progress narration.
evidence: A1, A2, A6, A7; feedback/human.md pain point 5 and section 4
tag_reason: Messaging style is mostly the Codex model's; the skills may encourage a recap line, but that cannot be told from the logs.

summary: Agent and release messages used jargon a business user did not understand: 'signed financial lines', 'first observed', 'one-penny tolerance', and 'No packaging Git commit exists; producing-file checksums are recorded'.
evidence: A2, A5, A7; feedback/human.md section 4; human/notes.md Turn 8
tag_reason: The packaging-commit and tolerance statements come from release and review helper output that the agent relayed.

summary: The 97.0% repeat-buyer revenue share appeared first in the draft without being shown in chat, and the user doubted leaning on a two-year measure that is close to true by construction.
evidence: A5, U6 item 6, A6; feedback/human.md section 5
tag_reason: It was an agent analytic choice (child question Q-009) rather than a clear workbench defect.

summary: The published data upper-cases stock codes (merging 47566b into 47566B) without any record in the publication, catalog or methodology; this moves Tea Time Party Bunting from 17.4% (rank 7) to 16.3% (rank 9).
evidence: Q4 spot-check: referee/spot.out, referee/spot2.out; project/data/parquet/retail_lines/2026-10-16-v1/retail_lines.parquet; project/investigations/marketing-investment/results/products-without-reversal.csv
tag_reason: The agent's conversion did it; whether the release's conversion guidance prescribes or should surface such normalisation was not inspected.

summary: The release folder nests under investigation and package names the user never chose, and the README mentions this only in its 'How it works' section.
evidence: A7, U8; feedback/human.md section 3; human/notes.md Turn 8
tag_reason: Folder layout and README placement are release behaviour.

summary: START-HERE lists methodology.md both as a file to attach to the deck builder and as internal, which was confusing on first read.
evidence: A5; feedback/human.md section 6; human/notes.md Turn 6
tag_reason: START-HERE comes from the package format templates.

summary: The README's headline-checkpoint paragraph is dense, install and MCP material sits in the same document, and it does not explain what 'answered' means or that status will not apply edits.
evidence: human/README.md; feedback/human.md section 3; human/notes.md Turn 1
tag_reason: The README is the release's user documentation.

summary: Setup first targeted the base interpreter and reported DuckDB missing outside the project, so the agent built a project venv by hand and then mis-installed DuckDB into the user site by resolving the venv symlink.
evidence: A1; feedback/agent.md 1.7 and section 3; feedback/agent-notes.md (initial setup entry)
tag_reason: The harness put a base Python 3.13 first on PATH, and the pip mistake was the agent's own; how setup picks an interpreter is product behaviour.

summary: The source register template's reference-link parsing guidance is disproportionately long for entering a normal source reference.
evidence: A1; feedback/agent.md 1.8; feedback/agent-notes.md (initial setup entry)
tag_reason: The guidance is in the released foundation templates.

summary: Status cannot record that a headline-only preview checkpoint is in progress, so expected missing draft files had to be explained by hand.
evidence: A4; feedback/agent.md 1.9
tag_reason: This is a gap in the release's checkpoint and status model.

summary: Helper output is verbose, with long absolute paths, and a result-only export returns an empty charts list while keeping the existing chart files, which is easy to misread.
evidence: A5, A6; feedback/agent.md 1.10
tag_reason: The output format comes from the released helpers.

summary: check-draft expected a slide order different from the user-approved one until the agent applied the presentation_order override, and gave no preview of the order it expected.
evidence: A5; feedback/agent.md 1.11; feedback/agent-notes.md (full package draft entry)
tag_reason: The storyline check is a release helper.

summary: Lifecycle text went stale (the project README still said no release was authorized after authorization), and scaffold guidance text remains in live state records.
evidence: A7; feedback/agent.md 1.12; project/investigations/marketing-investment/state.md
tag_reason: Scaffolded records and lifecycle fields come from the release templates.

summary: Exporting before the chart specifications existed failed with 'no specification in findings'; the agent asked for a metadata-only or dry-run export.
evidence: A5; feedback/harness-log.md (awb/package failures); feedback/agent.md section 3
tag_reason: The agent says the sequencing was its own error; whether a dry-run mode is missing is a product question.

summary: A reviewer subagent called the CLI with a --project flag it does not accept (exit 2), while the MCP tool takes a project argument.
evidence: A5; feedback/agent.md section 3; feedback/agent-notes.md (full package draft entry)
tag_reason: The argument shape differs between the release's CLI and its MCP tool.

summary: The Codex sandbox could not create heredoc temp files or the macOS xcrun cache, so several commands failed and were retried with python -c.
evidence: A1, A5; feedback/agent.md sections 2-3; feedback/agent-notes.md
tag_reason: These are Codex workspace-write sandbox limits, not workbench behaviour.

summary: The Codex backend returned 403 Forbidden on three reconnect attempts during agent turn 5; the turn recovered and completed.
evidence: feedback/harness-log.md (agent-005.jsonl errors)
tag_reason: A transient model-backend connection error unrelated to the workbench.

summary: The reviewer subagents spawned in A5-A7 do not have their tool calls in the parent Codex log, so their reads cannot be fully audited for isolation.
evidence: relay/agent-005.jsonl to agent-007.jsonl (only collab wait items); project/investigations/marketing-investment/package-reviews/
tag_reason: A logging limit of the harness's Codex capture, not a product defect.

summary: The persona front-loaded nearly all its context in U1-U2, including facts meant to be given only if asked, which thinned scoping to one round.
evidence: U1, U2; human/BRIEF.md
tag_reason: A known study limit of the persona briefs, kept for comparability with the Oct 15 runs.
